question: Detecting whether a task was actually handled by a defined code-reviewer subagent versus answered directly by the main agent matters for a monitoring dashboard the team is building. Which signals in the message stream reliably indicate that a subagent handled part of the work? (Select all that apply)
options: A) A ResultMessage with subtype "success", since only subagent-handled tasks are able to reach that particular subtype
B) The Agent tool result text containing an agentId trailer, which appears once the invoked subagent completes
C) A message carrying a parent_tool_use_id field, indicating it originated from within a subagent's execution context
D) Any AssistantMessage at all, since every AssistantMessage in a session is emitted from inside a subagent's context by definition
E) A tool_use content block whose name is "Agent" (or, on older SDK versions, "Task")
correct_answers: B) The Agent tool result text containing an agentId trailer, which appears once the invoked subagent completes
C) A message carrying a parent_tool_use_id field, indicating it originated from within a subagent's execution context
E) A tool_use content block whose name is "Agent" (or, on older SDK versions, "Task")
explanations: Incorrect. A "success" ResultMessage subtype indicates the overall task finished normally; it says nothing about whether a subagent specifically was involved, and it isn't exclusive to subagent-handled tasks.
Correct. When a subagent completes, the Agent tool result includes a text block containing an agentId trailer, which is a reliable signal that a resumable subagent ran.
Correct. Messages from within a subagent's context include a parent_tool_use_id field, which distinguishes them from messages in the main conversation.
Incorrect. AssistantMessages are emitted for every turn in both the main conversation and any subagent; most AssistantMessages in a typical session come from the main agent, not a subagent.
Correct. Claude invokes subagents through the Agent tool, so a tool_use block with name "Agent" (or "Task" on older SDK releases and in certain compatibility fields) signals a subagent invocation.
